text: Squeeze a spring, and it pushes outward. At crushing density torsion, the spin-made twist in spacetime, is proposed to push the same way. A negative torsion density means an outward effect, not less than nothing. Collapse then turns into a bounce, a change from shrinking to growing. Today's estimate is roughly a negative one sitting 70 places after the decimal point, like one whisper against an unimaginably loud room. The No Plots card stays beside our spring illustration. But how do we add up countless tiny spins?
